publicResults.footer: Memory published by the group on Goa.

about.title: The idea
about.lede: Private challenges for friends (or just you). Everyone logs; Goa does the maths and turns the round into a memory.

steps.title: Pick a challenge
steps.body: A film club, 30 days of reading, a habit, the bars in town.

steps.title: Everyone logs
steps.body: Ratings, pages, check-ins (each person on their own, from any phone).

steps.title: Goa tells the story
steps.body: Rankings, the thread and a page of highlights, ready to keep or share.

features.title: Libraries
features.body: Films, books, places or your own lists. Items keep their history across rounds.

features.title: Sealed ratings
features.body: Ratings stay hidden until the group reveals them together.

features.title: The thread
features.body: The round drawn as one line per person, plus pages you can download.

features.title: Private by default
features.body: Groups are private. A public link is anonymous unless each person agrees.

ranking: Only the order uses the Goa score: it breaks ties using each person's own history, a 5 from someone who rarely gives one counts a little more.
New people and new titles simply get the average. Hidden ratings never move a number you see.
about.byline: A personal project by Eduardo Dourado, grown out of the spreadsheets of a film club and a reading club.
about.feedbackNudge: Have an idea, or did something bug you?
about.contactBody: An idea, a bug, a partnership or just hello: write to us, a person will answer.

feedbackPage.title: How can we improve?

explain.sum: Adds up every value recorded for this field.
explain.average: The simple average: the sum of all the values divided by how many there are.
explain.count: How many valid records there are.
explain.median: The middle value once everything is sorted (with an even count, the average of the two middle ones).
explain.completion_rate: Completed records divided by everything expected, times 100.
explain.bayesian_average: A fair average for ranking. An item with only a few ratings is pulled toward the overall average of the whole list, so a single enthusiastic vote can't put it on top. The more ratings it has, the closer it gets to its own simple average (the plain figure is shown underneath). Formula: (n × item average + {weight} × overall average) ÷ (n + {weight}), where n is the item's number of ratings.
explain.spread: How much the ratings disagree (population standard deviation): the higher it is, the more the group was divided.
explain.consensus: How much the group agrees, from 0 to 100 (100 means everyone gave the same rating).
explain.surprise: Rating minus expectation, using pairs where the same person gave both for the same item. Positive means it beat expectations.
explain.indicator_bias: The average of the items each person recommended minus the overall average, how well their recommendations landed.

wrapped.explainMinimum: Only shown once there are at least {minimum, plural, one {# record} other {# records}}.
